beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant at Kashimira, Thane.

Contracts are won through a competitive tender process: the client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, the contractor bids, and the lowest quote typically wins a letter of acceptance. The contractor then deposits a performance guarantee before site handover.

Major clients include Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation (MRVCL), MMRDA, and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India.
Revenue is highly concentrated: the top customers contributed 57% of total revenue in fiscal 2018, and Western Railway alone accounted for 52% of orders on hand.

The company claims competitive strengths in marquee client relationships, modern techniques (box pushing), a state-of-the-art RMC facility, and an experienced promoter team with over 20 years in infrastructure.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined over the five years reported: from ₹8,661.35 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a ~30% drop. The peak was ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015.

Net profit after adjustments (PAT) has fluctuated sharply: ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, ₹78.36 lakhs in FY2015, ₹32.63 lakhs in FY2016, a low of ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, then a sharp recovery to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) was ₹784.46 lakhs in FY2014, ₹945.78 lakhs in FY2015, ₹783.31 lakhs in FY2016, ₹676.19 lakhs in FY2017, and ₹928.80 lakhs in FY2018.

Debt levels: Long-term borrowings peaked at ₹672.72 lakhs in FY2015 but fell to ₹133.09 lakhs by FY2018. Short-term borrowings rose steadily from ₹3,082.27 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹3,537.35 lakhs in FY2018, indicating increasing working-capital reliance.
The company acknowledges negative cash flows in recent years, though specific cash-flow figures are not detailed in the extracted portions of the filing.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra. He holds 7,495,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.

Other directors and key management: Bharat Kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh, and Mukesh Pandey each hold 300 equity shares. The CFO is Anchal Pachori (CA, aged 28) and the Company Secretary is Mohit Soni (ACS, aged 26).

Related-party transactions: In FY2018, loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors amounted to ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration was ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties stood at ₹324.3 lakhs.

The DRHP states that no director or promoter has been declared a willful defaulter by RBI, and there are no criminal cases filed against directors. However, there is pending litigation involving the company, promoter and directors – the filing does not specify details.
Two companies promoted by the promoter – Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited – were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 for non-operation.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector in India is highly fragmented and working-capital intensive, contributing roughly 8% to GDP (at constant prices).
Market size: India's construction sector was valued at US$ 400 billion in 2015 and is projected to reach US$ 1 trillion by 2025, per the filing.
Growth is driven by government flagship programmes (Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India, Power for All), eased FDI norms in construction development, rising urbanisation and disposable incomes.
The logistics sector – closely tied to infrastructure – grew at a CAGR of 10.5% and was expected to reach US$ 215 billion by 2020.
Headwinds the filing itself lists: slow pace of government projects, working-capital constraints that can hit profitability, and changes in government policies.
The sector is competitive, with both organised and unorganised players; no specific named competitors are disclosed in the DRHP.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild is an infrastructure and construction company that builds railway platforms, bridges, roads and operates a ready-mix concrete plant – all concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra.
It derives most of its revenue from government and PSU clients, especially Western Railways, which accounted for 52% of the order book as of the filing date.
The company is raising ₹44.28 lakh equity shares (face value ₹10 each) in a fresh-issue IPO on the SME Board, with the price still to be determined. Proceeds will go mainly toward working capital.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined. There is no offer-for-sale component.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
Proceeds are allocated primarily to working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and the remainder to general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).
The company has not appointed an independent agency for project appraisal, nor a monitoring agency for fund deployment – the Audit Committee will oversee use of proceeds.

beats.beat: Client concentration: Indian Railways (primarily Western Railway) contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018 and 52% of the order book. Loss of this client would cause a severe revenue drop.
Dependence on bid acceptance: revenues depend on winning government tenders through a lowest-quote process. Failure to win bids or accepting lower values directly impacts financials.
Negative cash flows: The filing acknowledges negative cash flow in recent years, though amounts are not disclosed. Sustained negative cash flow could impair operations and debt servicing.
Repayable unsecured loans: As of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans repayable on demand. A demand for repayment could strain liquidity.
Promoter entities struck off: Two companies promoted by the promoter were struck off by the ROC for non-operation, raising governance concerns.

beats.beat: The DRHP provides certain accounting ratios for the company: EPS for FY2018 is ₹12.39, for FY2017 is ₹0.63, for FY2016 is ₹1.31 (all on face value of ₹10). RoNW for FY2018 is 28.14%, for FY2017 is 1.97%, for FY2016 is 4.14%.

A comparison with peer group companies is presented but the filing does not name the peers. The peer metrics shown include figures 12.39, 44.71, 28.14, and 6053.05 (likely revenue in lakhs). Without named peers, a peer valuation table cannot be constructed from the filing alone.

The issue price is to be determined in consultation with the lead manager; the DRHP states the price will be justified based on the above accounting ratios, but no implied price range can be computed from the available data.
